question: When shadowing the chief executive in an internal meeting, can I just post a quick, definite answer in the chat, and where does the value that backs this sit among our company values?

sources.quote: Still, our [Results for Customers value](/handbook/values/#operate-with-a-bias-for-action) mentions to operate with a bias for action.
Results for Customers is at the top of our values hierarchy, as our customers achieving results drives overall business performance that enables everything else.

note: The shadow page allows a quick answer citing the bias-for-action part of Results for Customers; the values page says that value is at the top of the hierarchy.

check.changes: Tightened part 2: removed loose strings ('the top', 'top of', 'first in', bare 'highest') that match unrelated text.

question: I'm covering my boss's job while I work toward being promoted into it. What is that kind of temporary title called, and do I get extra pay for it?

sources.quote: **Interim** means the individual is working on a promotion into the role.
For team members on a base salary compensation plan, your bonus will be an additional 10% of your salary for the duration of the interim role period.
For an interim role to be considered, the need for coverage would need to be longer than a 30 day time period.

note: Leadership defines the title (Interim = working on a promotion into the role); Total Rewards gives the pay (extra 10% of salary if the cover lasts over 30 days).

question: If I get promoted in the promotion round held in the fourth quarter, when does it take effect, and who gets to read the write-up about my promotion?

sources.quote: **Q4 Cycle:** Promotions effective November 1
which is why every promotion document at GitLab is shared with the entire company and uses the values as its core structure.

note: Total Rewards gives the effective date of the fourth-quarter promotion cycle; the values page says every promotion document is shared with the entire company.

check.changes: Question named the round more precisely (the fourth-quarter promotion round), since 'end-of-year' could mean the annual review; removed loose part-2 strings ('everyone', 'the company').

question: On what day of the month is the company-wide call that opens the next monthly release, and on what day does a product milestone end?

sources.quote: On the 8th of each month (or the next business day), we have a kickoff meeting
Set the end date to be the Friday prior to the third Thursday of the release month

answer_parts: Friday prior to the third Thursday
note: Communication gives the kickoff date (the 8th); Product gives the milestone end (the Friday before the third Thursday of the release month).

check.changes: Question no longer reuses 'kickoff'; '8th' could match 18th/28th; 'third Thursday' alone matched the wrong answer (release day), now requires the Friday before it.

question: How often does our chief executive meet with people who report to his direct reports, and how often does he sit down with his leaders about the main goals and numbers?

sources.quote: The CEO conducts quarterly skip-level meetings with all indirect reports.
I like to meet regularly (weekly) to talk about top priorities and our progress on key metrics.

note: Leadership says the CEO holds skip-levels quarterly; the CEO page says he meets weekly on priorities and key metrics.

question: When I hold a meeting with the people who report to my direct reports, should it be recorded? And for meetings I do record to the Zoom cloud, what exactly do I put in the meeting title so the video lands in the shared Google Drive folder?

sources.quote: The skip level meeting is never recorded as it is a way to build trust with the team members.
you must include the text `[REC]` in the meeting title if you want them to be automatically placed in the `GitLab Videos Recorded` folder in Google Drive on an hourly basis

note: Leadership says skip-level meetings are never recorded; Communication explains the [REC] title tag that would otherwise push the recording to Drive.

check.changes: Question now asks for the title text explicitly (the old one only said 'the tag', so the Communication part was not tested); bare 'REC' matched 'recorded', replaced with bracketed/quoted forms.

question: As the chief executive's shadow on customer calls, how do I let him know when he uses a phrase that makes him sound unsure, and how long will those messages be kept?

sources.quote: When attending **external meetings**, notify the CEO in a private Zoom chat message when the CEO uses the phrase `I think`.
Zoom Chat has been configured for a 30 day retention.

note: The shadow page says to flag it in a private Zoom chat; Communication says Zoom chat is kept for 30 days.

check.changes: Question reused 'hedge' (the shadow page links 'Hedge words'); reworded.

question: After a webinar that the chief executive hosts, who is supposed to do the wrap-up and publishing steps, and is that group active right now?

sources.quote: When there's a webinar with the CEO, it is expected that the [CEO Shadows](/handbook/ceo/shadow/) execute the steps outlined in the `when the webinar is over` paragraph.
The CEO shadow program is on hold until further notice.

note: The webinar page assigns the post-webinar steps to the CEO Shadows; the CEO page says that program is on hold until further notice.

question: A teammate just became a mother. As her manager, can I buy a present for the newborn and claim it back, and how much paid leave will she get?

sources.quote: Baby gifts are not reimbursable as GitLab already sends them a [gift](/handbook/people-group/celebrations/#new-parent-swag).
you'll have 16 weeks of paid leave to bond with your new family member

note: Finance says baby gifts can't be expensed because the company already sends one; Total Rewards gives 16 weeks of paid parental leave.

check.changes: Question reused 'baby' + 'gift' from the finance quote; reworded.

question: Roughly what share of people end up with the top performance rating, and how far can my rating push the company bonus up or down from its target?

sources.quote: typically organizations have ~25% of team members "exceeding", 60-65% "performing", and 10-15% "developing".
While the target is 10% of base salary, payout is commensurate with performance rating and budget and may pay between 80% - 120% of target.

note: Leadership gives the expected rating spread (~25% exceeding); Total Rewards says bonus payout follows the rating and ranges 80-120% of target.

check.changes: Part 2 accepted either end of the range alone, now needs both 80% and 120%; removed 'quarter of' (matches 'each quarter of the year').

question: Someone on my team is on a performance plan. Can the rest of the team see that plan, and how often should their manager be meeting with them about it?

sources.quote: Performance improvement plans, disciplinary actions, and individual feedback are restricted, as they may contain negative feedback and [negative feedback is 1-1](/handbook/values/#collaboration) between you and your manager.
It is best practice for the manager to meet with their team member at least once a week to monitor and discuss their performance.

note: Communication says performance plans are restricted (limited access); Leadership says the manager should meet the person at least weekly.

question: If a release is running late, do we push the date back, and in which month does the big version-number jump happen each year?

sources.quote: If we have something planned for a specific date, we make that date.
But every one of them doesn't contain all the features we planned.
Our standard practice is to have the Major [release](https://about.gitlab.com/releases/) every May

note: Values says planned dates are kept and scope is cut instead; Product says the major version release is every May.

check.changes: Removed loose part-1 strings ('on the date', 'without all', 'not push'); added scope phrasings.

question: I'm based outside the US. Do I need receipts even for small expenses, and is 'international' the right word to describe people like me?

sources.quote: For Non-US Team Members, receipts are required for all expenses.
US-based team members should not refer to team members outside the US as "international". Instead, use "non-US".

note: Finance says team members outside the US need receipts for every expense; Communication says to say 'non-US' instead of 'international'.

check.changes: 'all expenses' was a substring of the question's 'small expenses', so part 1 matched any reply echoing the question; replaced with non-echoing phrasings.

question: Are regular employees treated as insiders for trading purposes here? What changes if I shadow the chief executive, and when does the trading window usually open?

sources.quote: we declare everyone in the company as an insider, which allows us to remain transparent internally about our numbers, etc.
participants in the shadow program will be considered Designated Insiders because shadows have access to MNPI.
We anticipate that our quarterly trading window will open the third trading day after the

note: Values says everyone is an insider; the CEO page adds that shadows become Designated Insiders; Finance says the window opens the third trading day after results.

question: I'm a grade 9 manager. Can the company pay for an outside coach for me, how much development money do I get each year, and what do I need to note if I also expense a conference I attend for work?

sources.quote: Professional coaching by external coaches is offered for managers and IC's Job Grade 8 and above using the [Growth and Development Fund]
That's why we provide up to $10,000 each year specifically for your career development.

All costs associated with attending a conference to represent GitLab are reimbursable and an approved completed [G&D issue](/handbook/people-group/learning-and-development/growth-and-development/) will need to be noted in the expense report upon submission.

note: Leadership says grade 8+ get external coaching via the development fund; Total Rewards caps that fund at $10,000 a year; Finance requires an approved G&D issue on conference expense reports.

check.changes: Part 3 bare 'G&D' overlapped part 1; tightened parts 1 and 3.

question: I'm on a performance plan and have been in my current role for four months. Can I apply for an opening on another team, what's the normal minimum time in role before applying internally, and will my teammates be able to see my plan?

sources.quote: When in the process of underperformance remediation team members are generally not eligible for transfer to other roles within GitLab.
Time in role eligibility will be 6 months in current role.

Performance improvement plans, disciplinary actions, and individual feedback are restricted, as they may contain negative feedback and [negative feedback is 1-1](/handbook/values/#collaboration) between you and your manager.

note: Leadership blocks transfers during remediation; Hiring requires 6 months in role for internal moves; Communication keeps performance plans restricted.

check.changes: Hiring internal-hiring-process.md also says people under written performance management may not be eligible, so leadership adds no unique part: sections reduced to hiring + communication (leadership source kept as support). Part 1 widened to hiring's wording.

question: Who has the final say on how we price the product and which tier a feature goes in, and what is that person's name?

sources.quote: The CEO is the DRI for pricing and tiers.
This page details processes specific to Bill Staples, CEO of GitLab.

note: Product names the CEO as owner of pricing and tiers; the CEO page names him (Bill Staples).

check.changes: Dropped the Slack sign-off part: communication says Slack must not be used for approvals, but the CEO prefers Slack and product/groups/fulfillment uses Slack approvals (screenshot in issue), so that part was contested and its strings ('should not', "shouldn't") matched anything. Now CEO + name only.

question: I'd like to shadow one of our executives. Is the chief executive's program taking people right now, would shadowing the product chief help my case for promotion, and does shadowing the finance chief affect when I can trade shares?

sources.quote: The CEO shadow program is on hold until further notice.
The CPO Shadow Program is not a performance evaluation or the next step to a promotion.
Please be aware that the role of CFO Shadow will place you on the Designated Insider list for that quarter.

note: The CEO page says his program is on hold; Product says the CPO shadow program is not a step to promotion; Finance says CFO shadows go on the Designated Insider list and need pre-clearance to trade.

question: I just started. How much can I spend setting up my home office, how soon can I sit on interview panels, and how long until I can be considered for extra stock in the yearly review?

sources.quote: new hires will receive a 1,500 USD (or equivalent local currency) stipend to help you towards setting up your home office in your first year
It is typically expected for new hires to focus on and complete their onboarding for at least two weeks before being part of an interview team.
Team members may be eligible to participate in the annual refresh grant cycle review if they have completed six months of service with the company.

note: Finance gives the first-year home office stipend; Hiring says two weeks of onboarding before interviewing; Total Rewards needs six months of service for a refresh grant.

question: Can I still claim back what I pay for my own private secure-browsing service, or has that changed?

sources.quote: Starting July 15, 2026, GitLab no longer reimburses personal VPN subscriptions (such as ExpressVPN, Proton, Mullvad, and similar services) through expense claims.
Team members who need VPN access should use [NordLayer](/handbook/security/corporate/systems/vpn/setup/), GitLab's company-provisioned VPN solution

note: Old: personal VPN subscriptions could be expensed; new: from July 15, 2026 they are not reimbursed and team members use the company VPN, NordLayer.

question: Can I sign up to spend a couple of weeks following our chief executive around to all his meetings?

sources.quote: The CEO shadow program is on hold until further notice.

note: Old: team members could join a rotation shadowing the CEO; new: the CEO shadow program is on hold until further notice.

question: Where should I post company news that isn't urgent and doesn't affect most people? I remember an old general announcements channel - what replaced it?

sources.quote: **The above should all go in the new #whats-happening-at-GitLab channel** (formerly the `#company-announcement` channel).

note: Old: such posts went to #company-announcement; new: that channel is now #whats-happening-at-GitLab.

question: What do we call it now when people get moved between teams to fix priorities, didn't it used to have a fancier name, and did renaming it make any difference?

sources.quote: The last example is when we used 'Prioritizing for Global Optimization' for what we renamed to headcount reset.
we saw a good reduction in the use of this disruptive practice of moving people around.

note: Old name: 'Prioritizing for Global Optimization'; new name: 'headcount reset', and after the rename the practice was used less.

question: For the coding interview, will a candidate be asked to fix an actual open bug or feature request from our product backlog?

sources.quote: It's also worth noting and making the candidate aware that we no longer request that they work on live or "real" issues as part of the technical interview.
the merge request we send is self-contained and drawn from a curated bank of technical exercises.

note: Old: candidates worked on live or real issues; new: they get a self-contained merge request from a curated bank of exercises.

check.changes: Question reused 'real'/'live' issue wording; reworded. Added curated/self-contained phrasings.

question: I work for the UK part of the company and only joined a couple of months ago. Can I already take the legal paternity leave, or do I have to wait?

sources.quote: Effective 6 April 2026, eligibility for Statutory Paternity Leave starts from a team member's first day of employment. The previous requirement of 26 weeks of continuous service is abolished.

note: Old: 26 weeks of continuous service were needed; new: since 6 April 2026 eligibility starts on the first day of employment.

question: When a one-off bonus is set in dollars, what rate is used to turn it into my local currency? Is it the monthly rate?

sources.quote: will be converted to local currency using the set exchange rates above.
This is a reversion of the prior policy put in place to use monthly rates with the reversion going into effect as of September 1, 2023.

note: Old: one-time USD bonuses were converted at monthly rates; new: since September 1, 2023 the policy reverted to the set exchange rates.

question: Can everybody see the pay range for their own job now, or is that still only in some countries?

sources.quote: As of May 1, 2026, all team members at GitLab, regardless of location, have visibility to their compensation range in Workday.

note: Starting May 1, 2026 every team member, in every location, can see their own compensation range in Workday.

question: Is the old fast-response process for urgent problems that need people from across engineering still how we handle those, or was it swapped for something else?

note: Old: a longer list of values; new: condensed into the six CREDIT values plus operating principles because the old list was hard to remember.
